ef.caveat: Every rule here is in our public register, with a reference to the legal act. A licensed accountant is still checking the values.
ef.law.p1: Today e-Factura is mandatory in four cases: supplies to state institutions and in public procurement, supplies to agents with no fiscal relationship with the budget (since 1 January 2025), supplies for the projects named in art. 104(c¹) of the Tax Code, and companies that SFS has put on its risk list.
ef.law.p2: International VAT trackers wrote that e-Factura would become mandatory for every company on 1 October 2026. That date has passed, and as of 15 October 2026 no Moldovan legal act sets it: for every other VAT payer, e-Factura remains optional. The list of companies that must use it grows through SFS orders; the latest, Order 494 of 2 October 2026, added six companies. If an obligation for everyone is adopted, we’ll add it to the register and say so here.
ef.law.p3: From 1 January 2026 the rule that denied a buyer the VAT deduction on a paper invoice from a listed supplier was repealed.
ef.law.p4: A VAT refund is capped at a share of the VAT that buyers paid, documented through e-Factura and through cash registers connected to MEV. Government Decision 496/2025 raised that share from 20% to 70% from 14 August 2025.

faq.a1: Not yet. Konta has the sales and purchase VAT registers that TVA12 is built from, but not the return’s form. We will call it done only when it matches, field by field, returns actually filed by real companies. Until then we do not say Konta does TVA12.
faq.a10: No. Neither the app nor the site loads analytics, screen-recording or any other third-party scripts. The Content Security Policy (CSP) both send lets the browser run only their own scripts. You can check this yourself in the browser’s Network tab.
faq.a2: For rates, thresholds, accounts and deadlines, yes. No rate is written into Konta’s code: it reads them from a public register in which each value carries the date it applies from and the act it comes from. Filing and payment deadlines are in the same register, each with its act and article, and the tax calendar on this site shows them month by month. A licensed accountant is still reviewing the register. In the app, a deadline calendar for each company is still to come.
faq.a3: Nobody, without the company director’s consent. When support needs to see something, it asks for access; the director grants it in the “Acces Konta” tab, read-only and for a limited time, can close it at any moment, and the access appears in the company’s audit trail. There is one exception, for emergencies: the platform owner can open access without consent, with a written reason and for at most a day. That too is recorded in the company’s trail, and the directors get an email. The database enforces these rules, not only the app.
faq.a4: The database. Every table holding client data carries the company’s identifier and is protected by PostgreSQL’s row-level security: a query sees only the rows of the companies the signed-in person has access to, even if the code forgets a filter. The app connects with a role that cannot bypass this rule, and an automated test fails if a table appears without it.
faq.a5: No. The database refuses to change or delete an entry, a posted invoice or a payment. A mistake is corrected by a reversal and a new entry, both in plain sight. Nothing enters a closed month; reopening one needs a reason and stays in the audit trail. The audit trail is a hash chain, so a row changed behind its back shows up when the chain is verified. Planned: publishing the chain’s head somewhere we cannot rewrite, so that not even we could rewrite the whole chain unnoticed.
faq.a6: Today the app is a preview, with no real client data, on a server rented from our hosting provider. The same provider holds the konta.md site and the mailboxes the app sends its mail through. Nobody else processes data: neither the app nor the site loads anything from third parties. Before the first pilot client, the app moves to a separate production server in the European Union, with backups encrypted before they leave the server and copied daily to Moldova. The Security page keeps the list current.
faq.a7: Not yet. One-click full export is one of the conditions we meet before the first pilot client: the books, documents and attachments as .xlsx and JSON, plus the original files, at any time and free of charge. Without it, “your data stays yours” would just be a phrase.
faq.a8: We have decided this: if Konta stops, customers get at least six months’ notice, during which they can read their data and export all of it. Accounting records are kept for years, so nobody should be left without them. The guarantee goes into the terms of service before the first pilot client. It rests on export, which does not exist yet.
faq.a9: No, and we will not ask for them. Konta does not keep your SFS portal password, your bank login or your electronic signature: you sign yourself. For e-Factura, Konta will use an API user that you create in SIA e-Factura. Such a user can do anything e-Factura allows, so we will keep it encrypted, and every use will appear in the company’s trail. Bank statements will be imported from a file.

priv.basis.p1: We answer because you wrote to us: answering a message we receive is our legitimate interest, and you are expecting that answer. When you ask for a demo or an offer, the processing is a step we take at your request before a possible contract. Limiting messages by IP address protects the form from abuse, also in our legitimate interest. You can object at any time to processing based on our legitimate interest.
priv.basis.p2: The bases are those in art. 6(1)(b) and (f) of Law No. 195/2024 on personal data protection, in force since 23 August 2026.
priv.changes.p: If we change how we use data, we update this page and the date above. A change that would need new consent does not apply without it.
priv.cookies.p1: The site uses no analytics, tracking or advertising tools and loads nothing from other sites. In your browser it keeps only the language and theme you choose: the konta_lang and konta_theme cookies, with konta_lang_at and konta_theme_at recording when you chose. They are shared with app.konta.md, so the app opens in the same language and theme, and they last a year. The same two values are also kept in the browser's storage (konta.lang, konta.theme).
priv.keep.p1: Messages and enquiries that do not lead to working together: at most 12 months after the last exchange, then we delete them. If the conversation becomes a contract, the contract documents are kept as long as the law requires.
priv.keep.p2: The counter that limits messages keeps your IP address for at most an hour after your last attempt, then deletes it.

priv.p1: In short: we use what you send through the contact form to answer you and, if you ask for a demo, to contact you about Konta. We do not sell it or pass it to anyone for marketing, and the site does not track you.
priv.rights.p1: Under Law No. 195/2024 (art. 15-21) you can ask what data we hold about you and get a copy, ask us to correct or delete it or to restrict its processing, have it given to you in a format you can use elsewhere, and object to processing based on our legitimate interest. Write to mail@konta.md: we answer within one working day.
priv.rights.p2: You also have the right to complain to the National Center for Personal Data Protection of the Republic of Moldova or to go to court.

priv.to.p1: Our hosting and email provider: the site, the form and the mailbox your message arrives in are with them.
priv.to.p2: The Konta app’s database (app.konta.md): every message also arrives there, as an enquiry we follow until it is answered. The app’s server is currently rented from the same hosting provider.

priv.what.p1: The contact form: your name, email address and message (required), your company and phone number (optional), the topic you pick from the list, and the language you were reading the page in. We use them to answer you and, if you ask for a demo, to contact you about Konta. Without a name, an email address and a message we cannot answer you; the rest you give only if you want to. priv.what.p2: The IP address the form is sent from. The server uses it to limit how many messages can be sent, at most five an hour from one address, so the form cannot be used for spam. We also pass it to the Konta app with your message, for the same limit.
priv.what.p3: If you email or call us directly, we receive only what you tell or send us there.

sec.d1.h: Each company’s data kept apart by the database
sec.d1.p: Every table holding client data is protected by PostgreSQL’s row-level security. Someone without access to a company does not see its rows, even if the app gets it wrong. The app connects with a role that cannot bypass the rule, and a test fails if an unprotected table appears.
sec.d10.p: The app and the site send a Content Security Policy (CSP) that lets the browser run only their own scripts and does not let other sites frame their pages. Connections are HTTPS only.
sec.d2.p: The database refuses to change or delete entries, posted invoices and payments. Corrections are made only by reversal. Nothing enters a closed month, and reopening one needs a reason.
sec.d3.p: What changes in a company goes into a trail in which each row carries the fingerprint (hash) of the one before, so a row changed behind its back shows up when it is verified. The chain’s head is not yet published outside Konta; see below.
sec.d4.h: Support sees your books only with your consent
sec.d4.p: The director grants access, read-only and for a limited time, and can close it at any moment. The one exception, for emergencies, can be opened by the platform owner, with a written reason and for at most a day; it is recorded in the company’s trail and the directors get an email.
sec.d5.h: A second factor, required for accounting firms
sec.d5.p: Every member of an accounting firm and every platform administrator confirms signing in with a code from an authenticator app. Without it, the server opens no company. A company’s own people are offered a second factor, not required to use one.
sec.d6.p: Each secret is encrypted with its own key, and that key with a master key kept outside the database and its backups.
sec.d7.h: Lockout, and confirmation before sensitive changes
sec.d7.p: After too many wrong attempts the account locks, and attempts from the same address are limited. Before roles, statuses or access are changed, the app asks for the second factor again.
sec.d8.p: The sessions page shows where you are signed in and lets you end any session.
sec.d9.p: The app and the site load no analytics, no screen recording, no fonts and nothing else from other sites.
sec.l1.p: As an extra factor, beside the codes from an authenticator app.
sec.l2.p: Somewhere not even we can rewrite, so that a trail rewritten from start to end would show.
sec.l3.p: Each client’s data encrypted with its own key.

cal.method.title: How it is made
cal.method.p1: Nothing in this calendar is typed by hand. The deadlines, non-working days and changes in the law are data in the public konta-rulebook register, each with its legal act, article and where it was published. The page and the feeds are generated from it.
cal.method.p2: When a tax deadline falls on a rest day or a public holiday, we move it to the next working day, as the Fiscal Code requires in art. 129 item 8), and check the date against the one SFS or CNAS published. The deadlines of NBS, of the financial statements and of CNAM's fixed premium are not tax obligations: when one falls on a non-working day we say so next to it, without moving it. Public holidays are those of the Labour Code, art. 111; a locality's patron saint's day is not shown, as it is a day off only there.
cal.method.p3: A deadline we found only in secondary sources is not shown with a date. It stays under "Deadlines we do not show yet" until we have read it in the act.
cal.method.p4: The calendar shows the general obligations. A company may have others, depending on its activity, its regime or an authority's decision, and statistical reports are filed only by the units the National Bureau of Statistics has included in a survey.
cal.moved: {date} is not a working day ({why}), so the deadline moves to the next working day. Legal basis:
